questions.q: Which of the following must be true before a journal can post?
options: It must have a control total entered
It must have passed validation, cleared any required approval, and have an accounting date in an Open period
It must use the Manual source
It must belong to a secondary ledger
questions.explain: Posting eligibility requires validation, approval clearance (if applicable), and an Open-status accounting date.

options: Updates account balances for every combination, period, currency, and balance type the journal's lines touch
Deletes the journal from the system
Automatically creates a reversal journal
Changes the journal's source and category
questions.explain: Posting is the step that updates the balances cube based on the journal's lines.

questions.q: Why can't you directly edit a posted journal's lines?
options: Editing is technically possible but discouraged
Posted journals are automatically deleted
Only the ledger's currency can be edited after posting
A posted journal has already changed real balances; editing it afterward would make those balances untrustworthy
questions.explain: Posted journals are read-only because they've already affected real balances others may rely on; corrections require a reversal instead.

questions.q: Can you post more than one approved, unposted batch in a single action?
options: No, posting is always one batch at a time
Only if they share the same journal category
Yes, several unposted approved batches can be selected and posted together
Only during year-end close
questions.explain: Manage Journals allows selecting multiple unposted, approved batches to post together in one action.

questions.q: Where does the actual posting process run and get monitored?
options: As a submitted process monitored in Scheduled Processes
It completes instantly on the Create Journal screen
Inside the approval workflow notification
It cannot be monitored at all
questions.explain: Posting runs as a submitted process you monitor to completion in Scheduled Processes, not an instant on-screen action.
